title: A separable root of a polynomial with p-th power coefficients is a p-th power
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, $E$ a field of characteristic $p$ and $L/E$ a separable algebraic extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $\alpha\in L$ and let $P\in E[T]$ be a polynomial [def-weil-polynomial-ring] such that (a) $P(\alpha)=0$, (b) $P\neq0$ and $P$ has pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure $\overline E$ of $E$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], i.e. there is no $\rho\in\overline E$ with $(T-\rho)^2$ dividing $P$ in $\overline E[T]$, and (c) every coefficient of $P$ is a $p$-th power of an element of $E$. Then $\alpha=\alpha'^p$ for some $\alpha'\in L$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 031V (lemma-pth-root, line 3747), part (2), and its proof (uses Lemma lemma-take-pth-root)

proof.text: ($P$ is separable over $E$.) Let $\iota:E\to\overline E$ be the algebraic closure of (b); polynomials over $E$ are viewed in $\overline E[T]$ by applying $\iota$ to the coefficients, which commutes with products and with the formal derivative $f\mapsto f'$ of [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. As $E[T]$ is a principal ideal domain, the ideal $(P,P')$ is generated by a monic $D\in E[T]$, nonzero since $P\neq0$, and $D$ divides $P$ and $P'$. If $\deg D\geq1$, then $D$ has a root $\rho\in\overline E$ ($\overline E$ is algebraically closed), so $P(\rho)=P'(\rho)=0$. Write $P=(T-\rho)R$ in $\overline E[T]$; then $P'=R+(T-\rho)R'$, so $R(\rho)=P'(\rho)=0$ and $R=(T-\rho)R_1$, i.e. $(T-\rho)^2$ divides $P$ in $\overline E[T]$, contrary to (b). Hence $D=1$: there are $U,V\in E[T]$ with $UP+VP'=1$, i.e. $P$ is separable [def-weil-coprime-polynomials].

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 031V (lemma-pth-root, line 3747), proof of part (2): the hypothesis (b) 'pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure', written out as coprimality with the derivative (cf. Fields, Section section-algebraic, line 3711, case (a): $dP/dT$ nonzero iff distinct roots)

proof.text: ($P$ has no repeated root in an algebraic closure of $L$.) Let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of $L$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] (every field has one); via $E\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$ it is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ containing $E$ and $L$. The identity $UP+VP'=1$ of step 1 holds in $\Omega[T]$. If $\rho\in\Omega$ and $P=(T-\rho)^2R$ in $\Omega[T]$, then $P'=2(T-\rho)R+(T-\rho)^2R'$, so $P(\rho)=P'(\rho)=0$ and $1=U(\rho)P(\rho)+V(\rho)P'(\rho)=0$, which is absurd. So no $(T-\rho)^2$, $\rho\in\Omega$, divides $P$ in $\Omega[T]$.

proof.text: ($Q$ has no repeated root in $\Omega$.) If $\rho\in\Omega$ and $(T-\rho)^2$ divides $Q$ in $\Omega[T]$, say $Q=(T-\rho)^2S$, then applying the ring homomorphism $\varphi$ of step 3 gives $P=\varphi(Q)=(T-\rho^p)^2\varphi(S)$, so $(T-\rho^p)^2$ divides $P$ in $\Omega[T]$, contradicting step 2. (This is the source's 'the roots of $Q$ are the $p$th roots of the roots of $P$'.)

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 031V (lemma-pth-root, line 3747), proof of part (2): '$Q$ has distinct roots in an algebraic closure as well, because the roots of $Q$ are the $p$th roots of the roots of $P$'

proof.text: (A common root of $Q$ and $T^p-\alpha$.) As $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, $T^p-\alpha$ has a root $\gamma\in\Omega$, so $\gamma^p=\alpha$. By step 3 and (a), $Q(\gamma)^p=\varphi(Q)(\gamma^p)=P(\alpha)=0$, hence $Q(\gamma)=0$ in the field $\Omega$. Further, $\Omega[T]$ is a commutative ring with $p\cdot1=0$, so its Frobenius is additive [def-weil-ring-frobenius] and $(T-\gamma)^p=T^p-\gamma^p=T^p-\alpha$ in $\Omega[T]$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 031V (lemma-pth-root, line 3747), proof of part (2): '$Q$ and $T^p-\alpha$ have a root in common in an algebraic closure $\overline L$'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Suppose $\alpha$ is not a $p$-th power in $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-x-pow-p-minus-t-irreducible] (with $F=L$, $t=\alpha$; $L$ has characteristic $p$), $T^p-\alpha$ is irreducible in $L[T]$. Now $Q\in E[T]\subseteq L[T]$, and in the principal ideal domain $L[T]$ the ideal $(Q,T^p-\alpha)$ is generated by a common divisor $D$ of $Q$ and $T^p-\alpha$; by irreducibility $D$ is a nonzero constant or $T^p-\alpha$ times a nonzero constant. In the first case $Q$ and $T^p-\alpha$ are coprime [def-weil-coprime-polynomials]: $AQ+B(T^p-\alpha)=1$ with $A,B\in L[T]$, and evaluating at $\gamma$ (step 5) gives $0=1$. Hence $T^p-\alpha$ divides $Q$ in $L[T]$, so in $\Omega[T]$, i.e. $(T-\gamma)^p$ divides $Q$ (step 5); as $p\geq2$, $(T-\gamma)^2$ divides $Q$, contradicting step 4. Therefore $\alpha=\alpha'^p$ for some $\alpha'\in L$. (The hypothesis that $L/E$ is separable algebraic is not used; the source needs it only for part (1).)

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 031V (lemma-pth-root, line 3747), proof of part (2): 'If $\alpha$ is not a $p$th power, then $T^p-\alpha$ is irreducible over $L$ (Lemma lemma-take-pth-root, Tag 09HF) ... Thus $Q$ and $T^p-\alpha$ are not relatively prime, which implies $T^p-\alpha\mid Q$ in $L[T]$. This contradicts the fact that the roots of $Q$ are pairwise distinct.'
